ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure gives in sequence four regional schematic maps of A, B, C, and D. A is located on the west coast of North America, showing a long and narrow peninsula; B is located near about 20°W, 66.5°N, and the island outline corresponds to Iceland; C is located near about 170°E—180°, 40°—50°S, and the outline corresponds to New Zealand; D is located near about 130°E, 32°N, and the outline corresponds to islands in southwestern Japan. Reasoning: The question requires comparing the types of plate boundaries near the volcanoes. B, Iceland, is located on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge and belongs to a growing boundary formed by plate rifting; A, C, and D are all located in the volcanic activity belt around the Pacific margin, and their volcanic activity is mainly related to destructive boundaries such as plate subduction and collision. Therefore, the one whose plate boundary type is different from the other three places is B.
